Shri Justice Sanjeev S Kalgaonkar

On The 7 th Of March, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 5527 of 2025
 Govind Dodiyar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ravi Sagre - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Arpan Jain Pl for the State.
 Order

1. This first bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of regular bail in connection with Crime No. 384 of 2023 registered at Police Station -Sarvan, District - Ratlam (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5 (L)/6 of POCSO Act, 2012 Applicant is in judicial custody since 22/06/2024.
2. As per the case of prosecution, the victim aged around 17 years and 2 months was enticed and kidnapped by Govind Dodiyar (applicant) and taken to Kundanpur on motorcycle and thereafter to Simroli.
The victim was recovered on 20/06/2024.
She alleged that applicant had physical relations with her.
The PS- Sarvan, District - Ratlam registered FIR for the offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5 (L)/6 of POCSO Act, 2012
The applicant was arrested on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6095 2 MCRC-5527-2025 22/06/2024.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted.
Trial is underway.

3. Learned Counsel for the applicant in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application,
submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter.
It is a case of teenage romance between two adolescent.
The victim had left her parental home at her own will and went to the applicant.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.

sentences.text: In her evidence before the Court, the victim (PW-1) stated that she left her parental home at her own will and went with Govind to Neemuch, where they got married.
She was aged around 19 years at the time of alleged incident.
Applicant did not compel her for physical relationship.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the remaining evidence by the applicant.
Further custodial interrogation of the applicant is not needed in the matter.
Jail incarceration would cause hardship to the applicant and his family.
The trial would take time to complete.

Therefore,
applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State ably assisted by learned counsel for the objector, opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
However, after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.

5. Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.
6.

The case diary and the material on record reveal that the victim (PW-1) stated in her evidence before the trial Court that she had left her NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6095 3 MCRC-5527-2025 parental home at her own will.
She was aged around 19 years at the time of alleged incident and the applicant did not compel her for physical relationship.
The veracity of the prosecution and the age of the victim will be considered on merit after evidence by the trial Court.
As informed, the applicant is a student aged around 20 years.
He is still dependent on his family and surviving on occasional labourer job.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of any criminal antecedent, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence or influencing the witnesses by the applicant or repeating the offence.
Further custodial interrogation of the applicant is not needed in the matter.
The trial would take time to conclude.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the young applicant.

However, the observations,
herein-above, are recorded for present application only.

7. Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforesaid facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, present application is allowed.

8. Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Govind Dodiyar shall be released on bail in connection with the crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court for compliance with conditions, as may be imposed by such Court under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C. 1973/ Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023,
to secure presence of the applicant for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6095 4 MCRC-5527-2025 trial.
9. This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the Trial Court may consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
